title: A small latte and a chat, please: Why this B.C. café owner put conversation on the menu
summary: Registered clinical counsellor Shane Trudell estimates one-third of the population suffers from loneliness — but many people aren't aware of it. A New Westminster café hopes to help.

image.caption: Amrin Satani is the owner of You N Me', a coffee shop in New Westminster that looks to reduce loneliness. (Submitted by Amrin Satani)

blocks.text: British Columbia
Registered clinical counsellor Shane Trudell estimates one-third of the population suffers from loneliness — but many people aren't aware of it. A New Westminster café hopes to help.
Counsellor estimates ⅓ of the population suffers from loneliness
Amrin Satani knows what it’s like to feel alone.
When she came to Canada from India in 2011, she didn’t know anyone. It was a quiet time in her life, she said.
"I know how it feels to have so much in your heart and not have anybody to share that with," she said.
That experience is why she started a business dedicated solely to making sure others have someone to talk to.

According to the Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA), 13 per cent of Canadians aged 15 and up say they are often lonely. While it affects all demographics, the association says loneliness can affect youth, seniors, people with disabilities and those suffering from addiction in particular.

items: As an immigrant, I know how it feels to be 'lonely and isolated' in my new country

blocks.text: Shane Trudell, a registered clinical counsellor and the clinical director of Nightingale Counselling in Vancouver, said few people seek mental health support specifically for loneliness, but it does often come up during appointments.
He estimates about one-third of the population suffers from loneliness — but it can be tough for people to realize.

"When you’re hungry for food, you learned a long time ago how to be aware of that and to go get a meal," he said. "With loneliness, most people are not aware of it. They feel this social hunger and they don’t know it’s something they should go and fix."
And, he said, the cure for loneliness isn’t one-size-fits-all.

For example, you may be busy at home but in need of connection with people outside the house, he said. Or, you may be dating and meeting new people all the time, but really seeking someone to know you more deeply.
Humanity Café
Satani had always wanted to help others; she planned to study medicine when she first touched down in Canada.
It turned out health care wasn’t for her. But that itch to help people remained.
In 2025, she opened You N Me' (Humanity Café) in New Westminster, B.C.
There, customers have the option to order a drink, something to eat and a conversation.
Amrin Satani chats with a customer at her café in New Westminster. (Submitted by Amrin Satani)

"It's for the days when you feel very happy, or you're feeling lonely, or you want to vent out, you want to celebrate a win, or simply you're just not feeling yourself," she said. "You want just another company and you feel that at least I had somebody whom I can just sit with or have coffee with."
Satani sits with customers who ask for a conversation whenever she can.
"I love it. It has no money attached to it. It has no finance attached to it. It has no tip attached to it, but I think it's the best thing people can buy here at the café."
While everything, including connecting with others, often happens online nowadays, Trudell said he’s encouraged by the concept of Satani’s café.

"I love that it’s something that’s in person," he said. "There’s kind of a high bar for entry. A person has to be willing to say, 'Hey I’d like to order a conversation.' You’re more likely to get people who are going to benefit from the experience."
